proposal.title: Ynthranae: a lightweight log monitor
proposal.summary: Ynthranae builds a lightweight log monitor for operators of public services.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Domain owners rarely notice certificates issued for their names by mistake. Operators of public services depend on certificate transparency every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a lightweight log monitor called Ynthranae. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Certificate transparency is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/ynthranae/ynthranae, which 188 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on certificate transparency for 9 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/ynthranae/ynthranae. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 102300.00 EUR for 114 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 2450.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Domain owners rarely notice certificates issued for their names by mistake. Operators of public services depend on certificate transparency every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a lightweight log monitor called Ynthranae. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Certificate transparency is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/ynthranae/ynthranae, which 188 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on certificate transparency for 9 years.

Deliverables and licence
